core.title: Author nothing before the operator ratifies the locked decomposition
core.given: A plan session whose decomposition the operator has not yet ratified and locked — the ratify gate, where LLM/operator judgment ends and deterministic authoring begins.
core.when: Any authoring writer would be invoked for a unit of the decomposition.
core.then: Author nothing until the operator confirms and the decomposition is locked.
prefer: On ratification, let the plan-session orchestrator (the system, not the agent) deterministically invoke the authoring writer per locked unit: complete, atomic, idempotently replayable.
In the session machine, keep the lock guard as the first statement of the author pass: while the session is unlocked, fail closed by raising an error before any authoring writer is invoked.
avoid: Invoking the authoring writer yourself, before or after ratification.
An author pass that invokes any writer while the session is unlocked, or a guard moved after the first writer call.
core.why: Ratify is the conversational-to-deterministic boundary; authoring only from an operator-locked decomposition keeps it complete, atomic and replayable rather than driven by unconfirmed agent judgment.
evidence: The stack's convention check for this rule passes.
No authoring writer invocation occurs in the session before the lock/ratification event; post-lock invocations come from the plan-session orchestrator per locked unit.
The session machine's author pass raises an error while the session is unlocked, as its first statement, before any authoring writer is invoked.
verification: Severity 4 (high); disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
Normative check: the session machine's author pass MUST refuse to invoke any authoring writer until the session is locked by the operator's ratification.

Fix direction: the lock guard runs as the first statement of the author pass, before the first writer invocation, and the pass fails closed by raising an error while the session is unlocked. The lock-state predicate, the guard-first ordering and the required fail-closed raise are part of the rule, not profile data; the concrete error type raised is a realization detail of each stack.

Scope: the check covers the session machine's author pass (located per layout.locations#session_machine) and authoring-writer invocations within a plan session; conversation about the decomposition with no writer invocation, and work outside a plan session, are out of scope.
Validator, detector and finding ids are realization details of each stack; the core names the check generically.

values: the session machine's author pass, in the files located by layout.locations#session_machine, is changed or reviewed

fires: The decomposition is proposed but not yet ratified, and an authoring writer is about to be invoked for a unit.
The agent is tempted to invoke the authoring writer itself instead of letting the plan-session orchestrator do it on confirm.
The operator has ratified and the session is locked: authoring must happen via the plan-session orchestrator per locked unit, not by the agent.
The session machine's author pass is changed or reviewed.
doesNotFire: Conversation about the decomposition in which no authoring writer is invoked and no locked unit is authored.
Work outside a plan session (no decomposition-to-authoring flow).

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (author nothing before operator ratification and lock; system-owned author-on-confirm; guard-first author pass that fails closed while the session is unlocked) is fully stack-neutral. Per the r4 mechanical check, no key is proposed anymore: the concrete fail-closed error type of the session machine (Bun: SessionGateError) is no longer bound through a profile key, because the closed v3 vocabulary has no map key whose documented scope covers runtime session-gate exception types (idiom.plan_syntax documents plan-artifact constructs and was rejected in audit r0; roles.runtime_components documents plan-executing components and their names/entry points/locations and was rejected in audit r2; idiom.error_types is text-typed and covers domain/boundary errors only), and v3 forbids proposing new keys. The core therefore requires the fail-closed raise generically (raise an error while the session is unlocked, guard as the first statement, before any writer) and keeps the concrete error type together with the concrete class, method and lock-flag names (SessionGateError, PlanSession.author(), self.locked) in bunOnly; instantiated with the bunOnly items, the obligation is unchanged — the required failure behavior, the lock-state predicate and the guard-first ordering stay in the core rule text and verification, not in profile data. The session-machine location globs from activation.facts[3] bind through layout.locations#session_machine; the path_glob fact is re-typed as a change fact (path_glob is not in the closed fact vocabulary). The corpus term ids (confirm_boundary, author_on_confirm) and the validator/test ids remain bunOnly. 'The authoring writer' and 'the plan-session orchestrator' bind to concrete stack commands through the tooling.commands#authoring_writer and tooling.commands#plan_orchestrator map entries. The lock-state facts need a new observer in every stack (observability needs_new_observer is preserved).
